subject: AI & Agents
title: Probability Over Certainty
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Probability Over Certainty.

hook.text: AI doesn't say 'this IS a cat.' It says 'there's a 97.3% chance this is a cat.'

buildup.text: Every AI output is a probability distribution — a ranked list of possibilities.

discovery.text: The model picks the highest-probability option, but alternatives are always lurking.

twist.text: Lower the 'temperature' and it plays safe. Raise it and it gets creative — or chaotic.

climax.text: Medical AI shows confidence scores so doctors know when to trust and when to verify.

punchline.text: AI deals in likelihoods, never certainties.

quiz.question: How does AI express its predictions?

details.summary: AI operates in probabilities, not certainties. When a model classifies an image or generates text, it assigns probability scores to possible outcomes and selects the most likely one, never being truly certain.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding that AI deals in probabilities prevents overconfidence in its outputs. A 95% confident prediction still means 1 in 20 times the AI is wrong.
takeaways: AI outputs are probability distributions, not absolute answers
High confidence does not guarantee correctness
Uncertainty awareness is essential for responsible AI use

faq.question: Why does AI express results as probabilities?
faq.answer: The world is inherently uncertain. AI models learn probability distributions from data. Expressing results as probabilities honestly represents the model's uncertainty rather than pretending to know the answer definitively.

faq.question: How confident are AI predictions typically?
faq.answer: Confidence varies widely by task and model. Medical AI may require 99% confidence to flag a diagnosis. Models can also be overconfident, showing 99% certainty on wrong answers, a known calibration problem.
